description: Optiver is a market-making trading firm whose interview process is built to find fast, calibrated decision-makers under pressure. The funnel is dominated by a heavy online assessment — a probability/sequence/reaction battery for quant roles and OOP simulation coding for engineers — and the quant loop centers on a live EV betting game where speed and bet-sizing matter more than ending profit.
note: Question block only. The site's answer body is not included here; the untouched page is kept verbatim in raw/<slug>.txt.

questions.title: Stock Transaction Sequence Counting (Catalan / DP)
questions.overview: A HackerRank counting problem framed as market-making transactions: count the number of valid buy/sell sequences that start and end flat without ever going negative. The canonical version is a Catalan number; common variants generalize to bounded transactions or arbitrary order sizes and are solved with DP.

questions.title: Proportional Allocation Strategy Backtest
questions.overview: A HackerRank simulation: backtest a momentum strategy that allocates capital each day proportionally to the previous day's positive returns, then report the average daily log return and the standard deviation of daily log returns. Light on algorithms, heavy on careful bookkeeping.

questions.title: Squirrel Nut Storage Tracker
questions.overview: An OOP simulation OA: model cone-shaped hiding locations whose level capacities grow Fibonacci-style, then support hiding nuts (deepest-level-first, with expiry) and retrieving them under a layered weight/percentage rule with a fall-down refill mechanic. Heavy on careful rule implementation.

questions.title: News Aggregation / Subscription System
questions.overview: The flagship SWE/SDE OA: implement a NewsProvider class that registers topic subscriptions with interest thresholds and per-second rate limits, ingests timestamped news, and publishes the right news to the right subscribers under sliding-window and priority rules. Most sittings allow about 75–90 minutes; a senior SWE variant allows two hours.

questions.title: Days Between Two Dates
questions.overview: A warm-up OA problem (often the first of the experienced/campus SWE OA, including a C variant): compute the number of days between two given calendar dates, handling months of varying length and leap years.

questions.title: Build Binary Tree from Edges / S-Expression
questions.overview: An OA coding problem (experienced-SWE rotation): given parent-child pairs as raw strings, validate the input against a priority-ordered list of error types and, if valid, output the tree's S-expression. The input validation is deliberately fiddly.

questions.title: Order Book Matching Simulation
questions.overview: A HackerRank matching-engine simulation: process a stream of buy/sell limit orders against an order book with price-time priority and return the sum of all executed transaction prices. Naturally solved with two heaps.

questions.title: Optimal Execution with a Broker Backstop
questions.overview: A HackerRank optimal-stopping / DP problem: buy n units one at a time, each at an i.i.d. price uniform on [a,b]; at each step you may accept the observed price or fall back to a broker's fixed price p, usable at most k times. Return the minimum expected total execution price under the optimal policy.

questions.title: Hot Air Balloon Festival Simulation
questions.overview: An OOP simulation OA: track balloons ascending/descending, compute additive wind speed at each balloon's altitude via a given formula, manage a stability rule (unstable above 15 m/s, regains stability after 300 s of calm), and report the stable balloons at/above the highest stable altitude. Timestamps are strictly increasing.

questions.title: PowerBank Rack & Cell Management
questions.overview: A 90-minute OOD simulation: implement a PowerBank with ordered capacity-constrained racks, time-dependent charged/depleted/spent cells, insertion, an equalization pass that swaps cells between adjacent racks, and a dispatch pass that drains charged cells while refilling vacancies.

questions.title: NASDAQ Market Data Price-Level Book
questions.overview: Maintain the AAPL order book from insert, modify, and cancel callbacks, then implement `GetPriceLevel(side, level_index)` to return the price and aggregate quantity at the requested zero-based bid or ask level.

questions.title: Design Circular Queue (Ring Buffer)
questions.overview: A guided phone-screen coding problem equivalent to LeetCode 622: implement a fixed-capacity circular queue. The interviewer leads you to recognize that the scenario needs a ring-buffer design, then has you implement it.

questions.title: Multicore Overheat Prevention Controller
questions.overview: Implement an OverheatPreventionController with lazy load changes, time-based thermal evolution under shared passive and per-core active cooling, automatic shutdown and restart rules, and status-delta output. The central complication is a cascading cooling decision: engaging active cooling reduces shared passive efficiency and can force additional cores over the engagement threshold.

questions.title: Thread-Safe Buy/Sell Without Overselling
questions.overview: A phone-screen coding round: implement buy and sell functions keyed by client, symbol, and quantity while ensuring concurrent requests can never oversell inventory. The follow-up extends the design to multiple buy/sell systems connected to multiple exchanges.

questions.title: OptiCargo — Cargo-to-Flight Scheduling
questions.overview: A phone/onsite engineering round (also an intern super-day round): given a long provided skeleton, implement order/cargo assignment to flights respecting departure-time and capacity constraints, with cargo splittable across planes. Heavy on reading large code, reasoning about correctness, and follow-up debugging/optimization.

questions.title: Design a Queue — Implementation Trade-offs
questions.overview: A phone-screen OOD round: design a queue and discuss how different internal implementations (array vs. linked list, circular buffer, etc.) trade off against each other in performance.

questions.title: Currency Arbitrage Detection
questions.overview: A HackerRank graph problem: given an n×n matrix of currency exchange rates, decide whether an arbitrage cycle exists after accounting for a small per-cycle transaction fee. The classic reduction is negative-cycle detection via Bellman-Ford on log-transformed rates.

questions.title: Satellite Message Propagation
questions.overview: A graph-simulation OA: model a satellite network where a message floods from Earth, each satellite forwards to its lower-id-first neighbors with a 10s-per-forward cost, then reports back to Earth after a 30s processing delay. Output the order in which satellites report back, with timing tie-breaks.

questions.title: Low-Latency Trading System Design
questions.overview: An onsite/super-day system-design round (SWE intern loop): design a trading system given a colocated 'locker box' next to the exchange while your traders work in an office in another city. The discussion centers on the network/infrastructure between the two sites and leans heavily on TCP/IP knowledge.

questions.title: HR / Behavioral Phone Screen
questions.overview: An early ~20–30 minute recruiter/behavioral call covering logistics (graduation, sponsorship, office preference), a project deep-dive with reflective follow-ups, and motivation questions. Largely standard and well-circulated.

questions.title: Zap-N Reaction & Memory Mini-Games
questions.overview: A battery of fast reaction / working-memory mini-games inside the OA. Reportedly up to nine games, though many candidates only see three. Each game accelerates as you progress; raw reaction speed and pattern recognition matter more than reasoning.

questions.title: Beat the Odds — Probability Test
questions.overview: The signature Optiver quant assessment: 30 multiple-choice probability questions, ~90 seconds each, no going back. You pick the answer closest to the true value, so speed and estimation matter more than exact computation. Wrong answers are penalized.

questions.title: Trading Betting Game (EV / Market-Making)
questions.overview: The core QR/QT interview round: a live betting game over many rounds. Starting from \$1000, you choose how much to wager across several sub-games (coin flips, dice sums, card products) given randomized odds each round, plus a market-making sub-game on the sum of three cards. The interviewer probes your sizing and reasoning; speed and decision-making under pressure matter more than ending profit.

questions.title: Number Logic — Sequence / Find the Pattern
questions.overview: A no-calculator aptitude section: ~25–26 number sequences in 25 minutes, infer the rule and supply the next term. Scoring is +1 correct / −1 wrong. Most candidates report needing ~15 correct to pass comfortably.

questions.title: QR Take-Home Data Project & Presentation
questions.overview: Mid-loop QR step: a take-home data project (often a modeling/backtest task on provided data) followed, if you pass, by a presentation round where interviewers drill into your approach, your pandas/time-series handling, and project decisions.

questions.title: Programming & Computer-System Knowledge Quiz
questions.overview: A multiple-choice CS-fundamentals section in the SWE/SDE OA: ~20 questions in ~20 minutes covering networking, databases, operating systems, multithreading, data structures and complexity. Single- and multi-select; no going back.

questions.title: QR Technical Round — Brainteasers & Estimation
questions.overview: A traditional QR technical round mixing probability/statistics brainteasers with Fermi estimation: invariant-style stone games, expected waiting-time questions, and market-sizing with confidence intervals.

questions.title: Market-Making Interval Estimation Game
questions.overview: A QR/QT interview game: across five rounds the interviewer asks a numeric estimation question and you respond with a closed interval [L, U]. You score 0 if the true answer falls outside your interval and L/U if it falls inside — so tighter honest intervals score higher. The target is reaching at least 2.0 total points.

questions.title: Likelihood / Event-Ordering Test
questions.overview: A newer OA section (appearing in 2026 sittings): read a chart or data table and rank three events from most to least likely. About 15 questions at a fixed ~90 seconds each. It tests data intuition rather than exact calculation.
